fix_prs.title: [CI] [AMD] diffusion/ming: Skip the CUDA-only fused RMSNorm test on ROCm

details.label: Status
details.text: `[FACT]`:
Both cases fail `assert (0 == 1)` (`kernel.call_count`) on both attempts, in every run that contains the commit (AL and AM).
The commit is in AL but not in AK (compare API).

details.label: Top hypothesis
details.text: `[HIGH]` [#46705](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46705) ([`4b43572e`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/4b43572e522912641ca7c83c5045f8c92bdad4c4)) added the test.

Its skip gate is `torch.cuda.is_available()`, which is true on ROCm. But `can_use_rmsnorm_cast_before_weight` requires `is_cuda()`, so `MingRMSNorm` correctly takes the native path and the mocked kernel is never called.

details.label: Disconfirming
details.text: (none found). The ROCm behaviour is as designed, so this is a test-gating defect, not a numerical one.

details.label: In-flight fix
details.text: ✅ [#47118](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47118) (open since Oct 28, **draft**). In its dispatched run [40739260895](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/40739260895), both cases are SKIPPED.

details.label: Suggested triage
details.text: get #47118 out of draft. Then confirm that the next rocm720/724 run skips the test.
